answer: When an agent submits a task, the ledger runs a deterministic “timber‑hash” over the output and stores it in a Merkle haven; any new submission whose willow‑derived hash collides within a configurable similarity window is automatically rejected, forcing the prover to produce a truly distinct result. To register a new identity the attacker must lock up a stake equal to the average computational cost of generating a unique output, currently 0.15 ETH per identity, and wait the 24‑hour challenge period before the stake can be reclaimed.
